It has been revealed that laLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

Industry observers note that javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

Recent findings suggest that the list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas indicates Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

Sources indicate that earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez mentioned Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

According to recent reports, tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

Sources indicate that the thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club stated Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

The same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas remarked the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

Industry observers note that the dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid said it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

Tomás González-Martín sostiene en El Debate que un presidente de LaLiga no puede dedicarse a atacar a uno de sus socios. Para sostener su argumento, omite una parte esencial: las acusaciones que Florentino Pérez y los canales oficiales del Real Madrid….

It has been revealed that pérez now faces his members. Their representatives will gather at Ciudad Real Madrid’s basketball venue for two assemblies called by the board, with remote attendance also possible. The only item at the extraordinary assembly is a proposal to ratify tennis player Rafael Nadal as a board member. The ordinary assembly opens at 9:00 on first call and 10:00 on second call, with Pérez’s report as its opening item.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a upcoming MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

While the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

In a recent development, the Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

In Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

Recent findings suggest that the parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an glitch in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

Recent findings suggest that in the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

According to recent reports, now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

Okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

According to recent reports, hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

  • The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the newly introduced head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

However, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some substantial money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Recent findings suggest that preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

Industry observers note that ‘That was the massive day,’ says a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective newly introduced head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

There was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is said to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

According to recent reports, media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

According to recent reports, there was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially confirmed Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is mentioned to have gone according to proposal as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his fresh job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

Sources indicate that the US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

In a recent development, pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

More players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

According to recent reports, responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ stated Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his fresh players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.

The Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.

Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was revealed back in June.

It has been revealed that the Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.

Sources indicate that just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.

Here's everything you need to know about the big game:.

Date: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160.

The Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals rapidly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.

Head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and upcoming signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit rapidly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.

The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.

"[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman said of the relationship with her teammates.

"I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday.".

Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but promptly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown. During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper remarked.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she said.

The Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime. The case adds to a growing list of criminal convictions for racist abuse of Real Madrid players in Spanish grounds.

In a recent development, the Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime. The Second Section of the Audiencia Provincial de Asturias delivered the verdict on 17 November 2026. It was a verdict by agreement, known in Spain as conformidad.

According to recent reports, the abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025. The fan made monkey gestures and noises in the 37th minute. Real Madrid’s players were celebrating Mbappé’s opening goal at the time.

The man will not go to prison as long as he keeps to the terms of his sentence. The term is suspended on condition that he stays away from football stadiums hosting official competitions for two years, Real Madrid mentioned in an official statement. The prosecuting parties also tied the suspension to a ban from LaLiga stadiums and a ban on approaching Mbappé. The defendant accepted these conditions.

According to recent reports, the fine was set at six months at a daily rate of €8. He is also barred from working in education, teaching, sport or leisure for three years and 11 months.

The case was charged under article 510.2.a of the Spanish Criminal Code. LaLiga filed the original complaint. It also supplied expert lip-reading evidence that proved key to resolving the case. Real Madrid later joined the proceedings as a private prosecutor.

Industry observers note that the ruling is LaLiga’s twelfth conviction for racism in Spanish football, Servimedia reported. The league presented the outcome as proof of its commitment to fighting racism.

The Carlos Tartiere has featured in this list before. In April 2026, a supporter was convicted over abuse of Marcus Rashford at Real Oviedo v FC Barcelona. That person received a nine-month prison sentence. Another conviction, handed down in September 2025, followed abuse of Iñaki Williams at an Espanyol v Athletic Club match from the 2019/20 season.

For Real Madrid, the verdict extends a run of cases involving its own players. The club has listed earlier convictions for racist abuse at Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and the José Zorrilla. The Valladolid case ended on 21 May 2025. The Audiencia Provincial de Valladolid convicted five people of hate crimes for abusing Vinícius Júnior at the José Zorrilla on 30 December 2022. Each received a one-year prison sentence.

It has been revealed that the pattern points to clubs and the league pursuing racist abuse through the criminal courts rather than leaving it to stadium sanctions alone. In the Oviedo case, the combination of a league complaint and lip-reading evidence was decisive.

Real Madrid is now acting as private prosecutor in other cases involving similar incidents against its players.

Tech Report: Trinity Rodman's non-negotiable for Washington Spirit: 'I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun'

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise.
  • LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized plan is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

In a recent development, "I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she mentioned Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

Sources indicate that five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

"I'm so excited," she remarked. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

"She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan remarked, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

Recent findings suggest that "I am excited to go in every day," Morgan noted. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

In a recent development, "We have these significant red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan said. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

Industry observers note that "I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman said. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many new players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

According to recent reports, "Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone mentioned. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

According to recent reports, before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a new construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

Recent findings suggest that "Obviously, it was incredibly vital for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

Sources indicate that "She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] Newly introduced York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

Industry observers note that "She's fun, she's engaging," Stone said. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

Recent findings suggest that rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

"Trin is a generational talent," Stone remarked. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".

Supreme Court makes CVC vote annulment final, but LaLiga’s December deal approval stands

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Football-espana

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club.
  • According to recent reports, spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation.
  • Industry observers note that the decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club. It is a legal win for the two clubs, but the later December 2021 approval behind LALIGA Impulso remains in force.

According to recent reports, spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation. The General Assembly resolution of 12 August 2021, which approved the deal, therefore stays void for good. Real Madrid and Athletic Club brought the winning case. LaLiga now carries the costs of the failed appeal.

Industry observers note that the decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote. In August 2021, Barcelona, Athletic Club and Real Madrid jointly revealed a challenge to the resolution. They argued it broke Royal Decree-Law 5/2015 and was passed through a highly irregular process.

According to recent reports, real Madrid described the annulled resolution as one of huge economic significance. In the club’s account, it was passed before clubs had enough information to judge the scope, impact and consequences of changes to the operation. The club also highlighted the court’s remark that LaLiga’s appeal tried to replace the Provincial Court’s view with LaLiga’s own self-interested view.

It has been revealed that laLiga reads the decision more narrowly. The annulled assembly approved the term sheet of the CVC project, and the appeal fell for lack of cassation interest. LaLiga noted the court issued a procedural order rather than a judgment endorsing the Provincial Court’s reasoning, and did not examine the substance of the case.

The deal itself does not depend on the annulled vote. LaLiga’s General Assembly approved the LALIGA Impulso project later, on 10 December 2021. Under the deal, clubs received around €2bn in exchange for a share of the value of the competition’s audiovisual rights over 50 years. A upcoming manufacturer set up by LaLiga and the fund manages that arrangement. Real Madrid, Barcelona and Athletic Club rejected it and stayed out.

Those December resolutions have survived their own court test. In June 2026, Section 18 of the Madrid Provincial Court rejected in full the appeal by Athletic Club and Real Madrid against them. It upheld the first-instance judgment of 19 February 2024 and ordered both clubs to pay the costs of that hearing. The court found that clubs still own their audiovisual rights, while LaLiga sells them collectively under the law. It also ruled that creating LaLiga Group International, owned jointly by LaLiga and CVC, did not breach the Sports Law or LaLiga’s statutes.

Recent findings suggest that that leaves the practical picture largely unchanged. Iusport, a Spanish sports-law outlet, described the Supreme Court order as having no practical effect on the LaLiga–CVC deal. The ruling still matters for how LaLiga is run, because it confirms that one of its assembly votes on the operation was unlawful. The league insists it respects court decisions and will keep defending the agreements backed by most of its clubs.

Industry observers note that the fight over the December agreements is not over either. Real Madrid has taken that ruling to the Supreme Court, which has not yet decided whether to admit the appeal.
